label: Affirmed Ghazali’s critique of dry rationalism while rejecting fatalistic quietism
description: In The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam, Iqbal praised Al-Ghazali for liberating religious intuition from Greek formalism, yet faulted him for separating thought and intuition.
dialecticalTension: Unites Ghazalian spiritual immediacy with active, world-making historical agency.

label: Engaged Nietzsche’s Übermensch while grounding self-creation (Khudi) in ethical theism
description: Iqbal admired Nietzsche’s critique of herd conformity and vitality, yet critiqued Nietzsche as "a heart that remained believer while his brain denied," anchoring Khudi in divine love.
dialecticalTension: Transmutes Nietzschean self-overcoming from godless power into ethical co-creation with God.

label: Formulated Khudi: dynamic moral and creative realization of the human ego
description: Iqbal’s philosophy of Khudi rejected pantheistic self-dissolution, insisting that human individuality matures through creative struggle, freedom, and love.
dialecticalTension: Redefines Islamic mysticism as activist self-affirmation rather than world-renunciation.

label: Inspired modern Islamic philosophical projects reopening dynamic legal and rational ijtihad
description: Iqbal’s call in Reconstruction for the "principle of movement in the structure of Islam" (ijtihad) deeply informed later modernist thinkers such as Arkoun and Abu Zayd.
dialecticalTension: Launches 20th-century philosophical critique of taqlid (blind imitation).
